title: Research
text:
Independent research project, funded by Fudan University’s Undergraduate Research Opportunity Program (UROP)
This project studies the impact of the 2003 Chinese Government Procurement Law (GPL) on firms’ technological innovation using a difference-in-differences design. The GPL is the first nationwide regulation of government procurement in China and mandated open bidding as the principal form of procurement, fostering a more open and competitive market.
My results show that the GPL significantly increased firms’ innovation in procurement-intensive industries, with stronger effects for more efficient firms. The effect is also more pronounced in more corrupt cities, and treated firms increased their R&D investment. These findings are consistent with the interpretation that, after the GPL, efficient firms were more likely to secure contracts and thus had stronger incentives to invest in innovation.
To support more granular mechanism analysis in future work, I have constructed a novel contract-level database that links procurement contracts to firm-level outcomes.
(Working paper draft in progress.)







Research assistant to Professor Jacob Moscona (MIT)
In this ongoing project, I constructed a comprehensive patent dataset with over 130 million observations using SQL and Python, and conducted data analysis and visualization on technology transfer patterns. I also carried out in-depth research on low-carbon energy industries, including solar PV and battery technologies, focusing on potential technology mismatches between rich and poor countries, and distinctive features of China’s cost reduction and innovation dynamics.



Research assistant to Professor Ting Chen (Hong Kong Baptist University)
For this project, I built a novel firm-level panel dataset from the Chinese Fuel and Chemical Industry yearbooks (1962–1995). I designed and implemented a data-cleaning pipeline that combines locally hosted LLM parsing, rule-based standardisation, and edit-distance–based matching to harmonise variables and firm names across years. I then linked yearbook firms to the 1985 and 1995 Industrial Census data to enrich the panel with additional firm characteristics. This archival dataset will be used to study the economic effects of China’s reform and opening-up.



Research assistant to Professor Xueyue Liu (Fudan University)
In this project, I assisted with a study on environmental regulation and firms’ low-carbon transition. My tasks included translating and proofreading the final manuscript and using Stata for data cleaning, analysis, and visualization based on the U.S. Occupational Information Network (O*NET) database. This work deepened my experience working with large, detailed occupational-task data and empirical analysis in environmental economics.





Broadly, I am interested in:

Government procurement, public policy, and firm dynamics

Technology diffusion and innovation in low-carbon and energy-intensive industries

Economic history and archival data construction

Applied micro-econometrics and data-intensive research designs

text:
这里会是我不定期更新的一些小笔记、想法和研究随笔。



Posted on 28 November 2025
Welcome to my website!
I created this site to collect my research, working papers, and notes in one place. Over time, I plan to share short posts about topics that interest me, such as:

government procurement and firm innovation

technology diffusion and low-carbon transition

data work and empirical methods (Stata / Python / SQL)

some thoughts from courses, seminars, or readings

Thank you for visiting — I hope this site can serve both as my research portfolio and as a small notebook of ideas in progress.
